newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: IMF says Portugal must cut spending for EMU.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Portugal must cut spending for EMU.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) believes Portugal can meet the budget deficit target for a single European currency but only if it takes tough action on public spending, the Diario Economico newspaper said on Tuesday.

Citing what it said was a confidential report, the newspaper said the Fund saw the need for a freeze on public sector wages, a reduction in the number of public servants and cuts in current spending by ministries.
"Our projections indicate that the mere freezing in nominal terms...will not be enough," the Fund was quoted as saying.
Antonio Pina Moura, secretary of state in the prime minister's office, told TSF radio he disagreed.
"We do not agree with the measures that the IMF suggests to guarantee budget targets," he said.

The government believed it could award wage increases slightly above inflation to civil servants without cutting jobs or raising taxes in 1997, and still meet targets for joining the European single currency, he said.
Cutting the budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 is one of the key entry criteria for the European Union's planned economic and monetary union (EMU).

Portugal's Socialist government, which is forecasting the deficit will fall to around four percent of GDP this year from some five percent in 1995, argues the EMU target can be achieved without huge sacrifices.
Diario Economico said the IMF report, drawn up after a visit to Portugal in July, said the alternative to real cuts in spending was higher taxes, something the government has consistently rejected.
It recommended a rise in Value Added Tax (VAT) as the levels currently applied in Portugal were below European averages.
